correctness.rationale: For finite tails, exact summation by parts gives S_N=sum j epsilon_j(T_j+T_{j+1}); Cauchy--Schwarz yields S_N<=4 W_N. The primary source proves W_N<=S_N for positive decreasing perturbations. The example epsilon_n=n^{-3/2} gives W_N=H_N and the integral lower bound S_N>=4H_N-16, proving optimality of 4. Hence boundedness of the source criterion is equivalent to convergence of sum n^2 epsilon_n^2. Standard integral tests then give p=1/2 and q=1/2. The source theorems convert convergence/divergence into the stated phase-transition/uniqueness conclusions. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The primary source identifies the speed of approach to the critical field as its central stability question and stops at the pure-power threshold gamma_c=3/2. The new theorem collapses its nonlocal criterion to an exact local weighted-square test with an optimal constant and resolves the natural second-order logarithmic boundary at that critical power, with an iterated-log continuation at equality. This is structurally useful for regularly varying perturbations rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
